youtube.description:
Corn flakes came out of the Battle Creek Sanitarium in Michigan, a health resort run by Dr. John Harvey Kellogg. He prescribed a plain, bland diet because he believed rich, spicy food inflamed sexual desire. In 1894 a batch of boiled wheat left standing went through the rollers and came out as flakes, and by 1898 the Kelloggs were flaking corn. His brother Will Keith Kellogg added sugar to sell it widely, and the brothers fought, including in court, for years.
